subject: Starship and Super Heavy descent and landing facts from the FAA LC-39A environmental impact statement noise study
source: FAA, SpaceX Starship-Super Heavy Launch Vehicle at Launch Complex 39A, Final Environmental Impact Statement, Volume II, Appendix C.1, Part 1: Starship Noise Assessment for Flight and Test Operations at KSC LC-39A (KBR, Inc., June 24, 2025)
confidence: primary (U.S. government document; trajectories, thrust schedules and operations data supplied by SpaceX)

vehicle_described.note: the future LC-39A vehicle, not the flown V3: ship 70 m, booster 80 m

facts.value: most of the descent is unpowered; landing thrust is applied during approximately the last 1,800 ft (about 550 m) of altitude
supersonic from apogee or deorbit until just below 75,000 ft (about 22.9 km)
facts.cross_check: IFT-4/5/6 webcast telemetry crosses 1,235 km/h at 22-23 km (data/ift_entry_corridor.json)

facts.value: west to east, like past Space Shuttle landings, with its own reorientation for a vertical landing
landing thrust occurs within about the final 5,000 ft (about 1.5 km) of altitude
supersonic until just below about 9,000 ft (about 2.7 km)
facts.cross_check: IFT-5 booster passes about 1,265 km/h near 1 km display altitude before the burn

facts.value: about t = 91 s at 77,000 ft, Mach 2.7, flight-path angle 38 deg

not_included: The SpaceX trajectory files (Starship_Bottom_Up_Ascent_Nominal_80_12_r2.ASC, Starship_Bottom_Up_Flyback_Nominal_80_12_r2.ASC and the landing files) are referenced but not tabulated in Part 1.
implication_for_exosphere: The single-burn catch lights at about 1,425 m of pin clearance with about 115 m/s of descent; the SpaceX-supplied landing profile applies thrust over about the last 550 m. A lower ignition is the published route to the about 18 s Flight 15 burn.
